heroHeadline: Mogadishu on Edge: Opposition Calls May 10 Protest vs. Talks — 8 Days to Constitutional Deadline; OCHA Chief: 'We're Choosing Which Lives to Save'
heroSubtitle: As of May 7, 2026, Somalia stands 8 days from its May 15 constitutional deadline as the political crisis reaches maximum tension. The Somali Future Council remained officially undecided on attending President Mohamud's May 10 dialogue, while the broader opposition bloc announced a mass protest march in Mogadishu for the exact same date — creating a direct collision between talks and demonstrations. The FGS simultaneously published a unilateral electoral timeline (Southwest State elections May 10, speaker election May 18, regional president May 23) that the opposition rejected as evidence of continued unilateral governance. At least 6 civilians were killed by Mogadishu police in Dayniile district's Warlaliska neighborhood during forced land evictions, directly fueling the protest call and deepening domestic anger at the government. Al-Shabaab continues to hold Adan Yabal in Hiiraan Region for Day 18 since the April 19 seizure, with the SNA counter-offensive still unexecuted despite President Mohamud's emergency order. At sea, three vessels remain simultaneously under pirate control: the Honour 25 (17 crew, Day 12 since April 25 seizure, pirates demanding $7M ransom), the Sward (15 crew, Day 11 since April 26), and the MT Eureka (12 crew, Day 5 since May 2) — 44 hostages total. OCHA chief Tom Fletcher appeared in Al Jazeera's May 7 gallery warning 'Things are really, really desperate... Often we're having to choose which lives to save': Somalia's aid programme has been cut from $2.6 billion (2023) to $852 million (2026), with 6.5 million facing acute hunger, 200+ health centres closed, and only 13.4% of the response plan funded. AFRICOM remains at 62 confirmed strikes for 2026 (last confirmed May 4, PR #36451).
footerNote: Data sourced from ACLED, OCHA, UNSOM, AFRICOM, EU EPF, EU NAVFOR, Combined Maritime Forces, UN Monitoring Group, and major international outlets. Casualty figures contested where noted.
